headline: Dallas Stars GM Jim Nill Is Facing A Major Test With Jason Robertson's Next Contract
take:
The Hockey News reports that Stars GM Jim Nill has handled Dallas's cap well, but that Jason Robertson's production could strain the structure when his next contract comes due. The same day, NHL.com's Tom Gulitti posted that Robertson scored the ninth-fastest hat trick to start a period in NHL history.

Our numbers say the production is real, if a touch hot. Robertson has 8 goals and 18 points in 15 games so far this season, and he's 2.31 goals above what his chances would predict. Expected goals measure the quality of chances, and his own sit at 5.7, so some of those 8 goals are finishing luck. The underlying play still holds up: DAL controls 56 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five when he's on the ice, and the team's share of the play is about 7 points better with him than without him. That's the kind of impact a team pays for, which is Nill's problem. Robertson went from 45 goals and 96 points last season, and he was drafted 39th overall in 2017, so the price has climbed steeply. DAL is 9-5-1, but its goals are 2.5 below expected and its goalies are 6.1 saved above expected, so the Stars need Robertson's driving to stay steady.
